intro: If you're searching for the best CETV advice near you, you're likely considering transferring out of a defined benefit pension and want expert guidance on the cash equivalent transfer value. You need a local pension transfer specialist who can compare your scheme benefits with the transfer offer and help you decide what's right for you.
need_heading: What people searching for CETV advice usually need
need_lead: Most people want clear, regulated advice on whether transferring out of their defined benefit pension is in their best interests.
needs: You have received a CETV quote from your defined benefit scheme and are unsure whether transferring is a good idea.
You want to understand how the transfer value compares with the scheme benefits you would give up.
You need advice from a pension transfer specialist because the transfer value is above the threshold that requires regulated advice.
You are looking for a local adviser who can explain the risks and benefits in plain language.
You want to know how to judge which adviser is best for your circumstances, rather than relying on rankings or ratings.
context: A cash equivalent transfer value (CETV) is the amount your defined benefit pension scheme offers if you transfer out. For transfers above a set value, UK rules require advice from a pension transfer specialist with specific permissions. Most people are better off keeping their scheme benefits, so careful comparison is essential.

Financial advice in the UK is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). You can check that any adviser or firm is authorised on the FCA register. If something goes wrong, you can complain to the firm, then to the Financial Ombudsman Service, and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may protect you if an authorised firm fails.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: Mention that you are looking for the best CETV advice near you, so we understand you want local, specialist help.
Tell us the size of your defined benefit pension and the CETV you have been quoted, if you know it.
Explain whether you have other pensions or savings and what you hope to achieve by transferring.
Let us know if you have any safeguarded benefits or special scheme rules that might affect your options.
Share your preferred location or area so we can introduce you to a suitable local adviser.
Mention any deadlines you are working towards, such as how long your CETV quote remains valid for.
questions: Are you authorised by the FCA with pension transfer specialist permissions?
How will you compare my CETV with the scheme benefits I would be giving up?
What risks should I consider if I transfer out of my defined benefit scheme?
How do you charge for your advice, and what will I receive for the fee?
How long is my CETV quote valid for, and what happens if it expires?
Can you explain the alternatives to transferring, such as staying in the scheme or using Pension Wise guidance?

faqs.q: Do I need advice to transfer my defined benefit pension?
faqs.a: Yes, if the transfer value is above a set threshold, UK rules require you to take advice from a pension transfer specialist before transferring. Even below that threshold, advice is strongly recommended because transferring is a major decision.

faqs.q: How can I judge which adviser is best for me?
faqs.a: There is no official ranking of the best adviser, so you should check that the adviser is authorised on the FCA register and has pension transfer specialist permissions. It also helps to ask about their experience with defined benefit transfers and how they charge.

faqs.q: What is a CETV and why does it matter?
faqs.a: A CETV is the amount your defined benefit scheme would pay if you transfer out. It matters because it represents the value the scheme places on your scheme benefits, and you need to compare it carefully with what you would be giving up.

faqs.q: Is free guidance available for pension transfers?
faqs.a: Pension Wise offers free, impartial guidance for people over a certain age with defined contribution pensions, but it does not cover defined benefit transfers. For defined benefit advice, you should speak to a regulated pension transfer specialist.
